title: I Took the Lapidary-Saw Booking to the Mentor Who Left My Slab on the Vise

parts.text: I stepped to saw two at 3:08 p.m. and mentor Oren was already cutting on my numbered slab. The board said: ONE SAW. NINETY MINUTES. SLAB STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-seven, shop member, holding a coolant ticket that listed our stone. Oren shrugged. "Mentors are the blade." I photographed the board, the booking, and his kerf on my vise. Then I asked for the saw log. At 3:16 the shop pinged why Oren's name was on my slab. I kept my voice shop-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A board is only a board until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop can see Oren's kerf on my vise during our booking.

social.video_title: He cut on my numbered slab in my vise — Part 1/2
social.description: Lapidary saw, a mentor on my vise, a ninety-minute clock he posted. I logged the kerf. Would you have asked for the saw log?

parts.text: Oren called it a trim until the shop asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the kerf still. The slab went back to my tray. Oren ran his own ninety and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about feed. Feed is a word mentors use when a booking exists. Saw policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE BLADE. I keep our slab on a labeled rack. Oren brown-bags his jokes. The saw finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Saw log, numbered slab, and a second line on the board. Was a trim ever my vise?
